title: In-process worker pool on worker threads
description: The first real worker implementation, and the one that proves the abstraction. A pool of Node worker_threads claims from the same queue over the same protocol as any external worker - it is not a special case or a fast path. This is what makes server-side evaluation just another worker rather than an architectural choice, and it is why the original server-versus-browser question dissolves. Worker threads matter specifically because the engine drives its generation loop on setImmediate: any CPU-bound scoring done on the main thread would starve that loop and stall the very run it is trying to advance. Pool size should be configurable through the evaluator params, hence through the auto-generated form.
acceptance_criteria: a pool of worker threads claims, scores and submits over the identical protocol an external worker uses, with no engine-side special casing; scoring never runs on the main thread and the engine loop stays responsive to pause and stop while a batch is in flight, demonstrated by a test; pool size is configurable via evaluator params; killing a pool worker mid-claim results in re-dispatch and the generation still completes

title: Pause a run when no worker can serve its evaluator
description: The operational failure mode of distributed evaluation, and the generalisation of what would otherwise be a browser-specific problem. If no connected worker advertises the run evaluator, jobs queue forever and the run appears to be running while making no progress - the exact dishonesty that genebaer-5ft was filed to remove elsewhere in the system. The run should pause with a stopReason naming the missing capability, and resume when a capable worker registers. Interaction to decide explicitly: a run paused for lack of a worker is legitimately paused, but it is still a non-terminal status, so the restart reconciliation added in genebaer-5ft will close it out as stopped on the next server boot. Decide whether that is correct - it probably is, since the workers are gone too - and document the reasoning either way.
acceptance_criteria: starting a run whose evaluator no connected worker advertises pauses it within a bounded time with a reason naming the missing capability, rather than queueing silently; registering a capable worker resumes it; all workers disconnecting mid-run pauses rather than hangs, and reconnecting resumes without losing or double-counting the in-flight generation; covered by a server test with no worker attached; the interaction with restart reconciliation is documented

title: Score cache keyed by genome and evaluator identity
description: Caching is both the largest available speedup and the reproducibility story for non-deterministic evaluators. Elitism clones the top N genomes verbatim into every subsequent generation, so without a cache those identical genomes are re-scored forever at full cost. And because model-backed scoring is not deterministic, a cache is what makes replaying a completed run produce identical fitness values. Persist hash to score in SQLite beside the runs table. THE KEY MUST INCLUDE THE EVALUATOR IDENTITY AND VERSION, not just the genome bytes: the same image scored by clip-v1 and clip-v2 are different numbers, and a key that ignores that will serve a v1 score to a v2 run silently and corrupt the comparison. It must also include the evaluator params, above all any prompt text, or two runs targeting different prompts poison each other.
acceptance_criteria: a generation enqueues only cache misses; with elitism=2 at least 2 individuals per generation are served from cache after generation 1; replaying a completed run with the same seed and config yields identical fitness values and enqueues zero jobs; two runs differing only in prompt do not share cache entries, covered by a test; two runs differing only in evaluator version do not share cache entries, covered by a test; hit and miss counts are observable

title: Worker protocol: claim, lease, submit, heartbeat
description: The wire contract between the job queue and any worker, in shared-types so server and web compile against the same definition. A worker claims up to N jobs and receives a LEASE with an expiry; it submits scores against the lease; it heartbeats while working on a long batch. LEASE EXPIRY AND RE-DISPATCH ARE MANDATORY, not a refinement: because the engine is generational it waits for every score, so a worker that claims jobs and then vanishes - a closed browser tab, a crashed thread, a laptop lid - would otherwise hang the run forever. On expiry the jobs return to the queue and any other worker may claim them. A late submission from an expired lease must be accepted only if the job has not already been scored by someone else, and must never overwrite a newer score. Note the parallel with beads own claim model, which already uses leases with lease_expires_at for exactly this reason.
acceptance_criteria: shared-types carries claim, lease, submit and heartbeat messages and the type-level suite covers their narrowing; a worker that claims and disappears has its jobs re-dispatched after lease expiry and the generation still completes, covered by a test; a late submission against an expired lease never overwrites a score already recorded by another worker; duplicate submissions are idempotent; heartbeat extends a lease without re-claiming

title: Worker registry and capability matching
description: Workers are heterogeneous - a worker thread running CLIP, a browser tab with WebGPU, a remote box - so the queue must only offer a worker jobs it can actually serve. Each worker registers with an id and the set of evaluator ids it can fulfil, plus liveness. This is the mechanism that makes the epic reframe true: RunConfig names a scoring CONTRACT such as clip-similarity-v1 and the registry decides which connected workers satisfy it, so a config never encodes where it ran. Capability must include the evaluator VERSION, not just its id: a worker running an older model produces scores that are not comparable with a newer one, and silently mixing them within a single run would corrupt the fitness landscape mid-flight in a way no test would catch. Track liveness so a worker that stops heartbeating is removed and its leases expire.
acceptance_criteria: a worker only ever receives jobs whose evaluator id and version it advertised; workers can register and deregister mid-run without disrupting an in-flight generation; a worker that stops heartbeating is removed and its claims are released; the set of connected workers and their capabilities is queryable; a run whose evaluator no worker advertises is detected rather than silently queuing forever

title: Job queue and generation barrier
description: Turn a generation of fitness requests into a set of individually claimable jobs, and resolve the generation only when every job has a score. This is what lets many workers serve one run while the engine stays generational. Each evaluation gets an id; each genome in it becomes a job carrying the genome payload, the evaluator id it requires, and its index in the population so scores can be reassembled in order. The barrier resolves when all jobs report. The queue can be in-memory: runs are already reconciled to stopped on restart per genebaer-5ft, so there is no value in persisting jobs across a process that will not resume the run anyway - but say so explicitly rather than leaving it implied. Scores must be reassembled by index, never by arrival order, or the population and its fitnesses silently desynchronise, which would corrupt selection without any error.
acceptance_criteria: a generation dispatches N jobs and resolves only when all N scores are in; scores are reassembled by population index and a shuffled arrival order produces identical fitness assignment, covered by a test; duplicate submissions for the same job are idempotent; a submission for an unknown or superseded evaluation id is discarded without affecting the live generation; queue depth is observable
close_reason: JobQueue with per-evaluation generation barrier; scores reassembled positionally; duplicate, late, out-of-range and unknown-id submissions all discarded; non-finite scores fail the evaluation rather than poisoning selection. QueuedEvaluator base uses its own operatorId as the worker-facing contract. 20 tests; index-reassembly and idempotency both canaried.

title: Introduce evaluator as a 7th registry kind with async batch fitness
description: The foundation for everything else in both epics. Two changes land together because neither is useful alone. First, add FitnessEvaluator as a new BaseOperator subclass and evaluator as a seventh OperatorKind, registered and resolved exactly like the existing six, so it gains registry metadata and an auto-generated params form for free. Second, change the engine so fitness for a whole population is requested once per generation and awaited, replacing the synchronous population.map over problem.evaluate. FitnessProblem keeps evaluate, visualize and compatibleEncodings - those describe the objective. Only execution moves to the evaluator. Ship a LocalEvaluator that simply maps the existing synchronous evaluate, make it the default, and keep all five built-in problems working with no source changes. CRITICAL COMPATIBILITY POINT: RunConfig.evaluator must be OPTIONAL and default to local. It is validated by zod in the server, persisted as config_json in SQLite, and saved to browser localStorage as presets - making it required would reject every existing stored run and every saved preset.
acceptance_criteria: evaluator resolves through OperatorRegistry as a seventh kind and appears in GET /api/operators; a LocalEvaluator is the default and all 5 built-in problems run unchanged with no RunConfig edits; the engine awaits fitness exactly once per generation rather than once per individual; RunConfig.evaluator is optional and existing persisted configs and localStorage presets still load and run; a rejected evaluation transitions the run to error with the reason instead of hanging; pause and stop during an in-flight evaluation neither deadlock nor double-apply a generation; existing core tests pass and new tests cover the async and rejection paths
close_reason: evaluator added as the 7th registry kind with FitnessEvaluator/LocalEvaluator; engine evaluates the whole population once per generation and awaits it. RunConfig.evaluator optional and defaulted so every pre-existing config and preset still loads. 10 new tests; batch contract and optionality both verified by canary.

title: Externalized distributed fitness evaluation
description: Make fitness evaluation a first-class, pluggable, distributable capability of the engine rather than a synchronous in-process function call. Today FitnessProblem.evaluate(genome) returns a number synchronously and the engine calls it in a tight population.map, which hard-codes both WHERE fitness runs and HOW it is scheduled. DECISIONS MADE: (1) evaluator becomes a SEVENTH registry kind alongside encoding, problem, selection, crossover, mutation and termination, selected per run through RunConfig and therefore configurable through the existing auto-generated form. (2) Workers PUSH: the engine enqueues genomes for an evaluation and any number of workers claim jobs and post scores back, rather than the engine calling out and awaiting a single evaluator. (3) The engine stays GENERATIONAL - selection waits for a complete, consistently scored population. (4) Full distributed evaluation is in scope: many workers of mixed kinds, server worker threads and browser tabs and remote boxes, serving the same run concurrently. KEY REFRAME: the registry evaluator defines the scoring CONTRACT - what the score means, which model, which version - while workers ADVERTISE CAPABILITY for that contract. A RunConfig says score with clip-similarity-v1, never score on machine X, so configs stay portable and server-versus-browser stops being an architectural decision. CRITICAL CONSEQUENCE: generational barrier plus distributed workers means a generation finishes at the speed of the slowest claim, so lease expiry and re-dispatch are MANDATORY - without them a single closed browser tab hangs a run forever. Separately, FitnessProblem keeps visualize() and compatibleEncodings, which describe the objective; only execution moves out.

title: CLIP similarity evaluator and its worker implementation
description: The fitness signal itself, now expressed as an evaluator rather than a browser feature. Implement a ClipSimilarity FitnessEvaluator whose params are the target prompt plus the model id and version, and whose contract is: given rendered image bytes, return cosine similarity between the CLIP image embedding and the prompt embedding. Because the epic separates contract from capability, the SAME evaluator is served by a worker thread on the server or a browser tab on WebGPU, and a run does not care which - the original server-versus-browser question dissolves here. Two efficiency points that matter regardless of transport: the prompt embedding is identical for every individual of every generation, so compute it once per prompt and never per image; and the model loads slowly and must be reused across generations and runs rather than reloaded per batch. Note CLIP resizes every input to 224x224 internally, so inference cost is independent of genome resolution - image size changes search difficulty, not scoring speed. The evaluator version must be part of its identity so the score cache never mixes scores across model versions.
acceptance_criteria: a ClipSimilarity evaluator is registered as a 7th-kind operator and appears in GET /api/operators with a prompt param that the existing auto-generated form renders with no frontend work; it is servable by both a worker-thread worker and a browser worker with no evaluator-side branching; the prompt embedding is computed once per prompt, not per image; the model is loaded once and reused across generations and runs; the evaluator reports an identity including model version that the score cache keys on

title: Image bit-string problem operator in a new vision package
description: The actual GA problem. It CANNOT live in packages/core: that package is deliberately dependency-light and its contents must never reach the browser bundle. Create a new workspace package, for example packages/vision, exporting an ImagePrompt FitnessProblem whose params are the target prompt text plus width and height, with compatibleEncodings set to binary so the existing binary encoding and bit-flip mutation are reused unchanged. Its batch evaluation delegates to the WS transport rather than computing anything locally. Implement visualize() to return the best genome as an image frame so the existing per-problem canvas path in the web app renders it with no new UI plumbing. Register it via createDefaultRegistry().register(...) and pass the registry to createServer, which already supports exactly this. Because paramsSchema drives the auto-generated form, declaring prompt as a string param is sufficient to make it configurable in the UI with zero frontend work.
acceptance_criteria: the operator appears in GET /api/operators with a prompt string param and the existing auto-generated experiment form renders it without frontend changes; a genome whose bit length does not equal width*height*24 produces a clear error rather than a crash or a garbled image; visualize() returns a frame the existing web canvas renders; packages/core gains no new dependencies

title: Pause a run safely when no scorer is connected
description: This is THE operational risk of browser-side inference and deserves to be designed, not discovered. With no tab open there is no fitness source, so a run has nothing to evaluate against. It must neither hang forever holding a generation half-complete nor spin re-dispatching. The engine or RunManager should wait for a scorer with a bounded timeout, and on timeout transition the run to paused with a stopReason naming the missing scorer, then resume when a scorer reconnects. Note this interacts with the restart reconciliation added in genebaer-5ft: a run paused for lack of a scorer is legitimately paused, not interrupted, but on a server restart it is still non-terminal and will be reconciled to stopped - decide whether that is correct and say so explicitly.
acceptance_criteria: starting an image run with no browser attached pauses it within a bounded time with a reason naming the missing scorer, rather than hanging; connecting a scorer resumes a run that was paused for that reason; a scorer disconnecting mid-generation loses neither the generation nor double-counts scores when it reconnects; covered by a server test with no client attached; the interaction with restart reconciliation is documented

title: Cache fitness scores by genome hash
description: Browser round trips are the bottleneck of the whole design, and elitism clones the top N genomes verbatim into every subsequent generation, so those identical genomes would otherwise be re-scored forever. Caching is therefore the single largest available speedup. It is also the reproducibility story chosen for this epic: inference is not deterministic, but a replay of a run that hits cache for every genome produces identical fitness values, so a completed run can be replayed exactly. Persist hash-of-genome to score in SQLite next to the runs table. Consult the cache before dispatching a batch and send only the misses to the browser. The hash MUST incorporate the problem params, above all the prompt text, or two runs with different prompts will silently poison each other with scores from the wrong target.
acceptance_criteria: a generation dispatches only cache misses to the scorer; with elitism=2 at least 2 individuals per generation are served from cache after generation 1; replaying a completed run with the same seed and config yields identical fitness values with zero inference calls; two runs with different prompts do not share cache entries, covered by a test; cache hit and miss counts are observable

title: WS fitness-delegation protocol
description: The browser must receive genomes to score and return scores, which extends the shared-types wire contract that both server and web compile against. Add a server-to-client message carrying a batch of genomes plus the prompt and an evaluation id, and a client-to-server message returning scores for that id. Ship RAW PACKED PIXEL BYTES, not PNG: the browser needs ImageData for CLIP anyway, so PNG-encoding in the hot loop is pure overhead and wasted CPU on the server. Watch the payload - population 40 at 64x64 RGB is roughly 491 KB per generation, against a maxPayload currently set to 1 MB in the websocket registration. Late, duplicate, and out-of-order replies must be handled: a generation is only complete when every requested score arrives, and a reply for a superseded evaluation id must be discarded rather than applied.
acceptance_criteria: shared-types carries the new message types and the type-level test suite covers their narrowing; a full round trip works end to end against a stub scorer; payload for population 40 at 64x64 stays under maxPayload or maxPayload is raised deliberately with a comment explaining the arithmetic; duplicate, late, and unknown-id score replies are discarded without corrupting a generation

title: Async batched fitness evaluation in the engine
description: FitnessProblem.evaluate(genome) returns a number synchronously, and GeneticAlgorithmEngine.runGeneration calls it inside a synchronous population.map. A browser-delegated CLIP score is async and carries round-trip latency, so fitness must be awaited AND batched - one round trip per generation, not one per individual. At population 40 and 200ms per call, per-individual dispatch would cost 8 seconds per generation. This blocks every other bead in the epic. Add an async batch path, for example evaluateBatch(genomes) returning a promise of scores, with a default implementation that maps the existing synchronous evaluate so all five built-in problems keep working untouched. runGeneration must await it while keeping the setImmediate loop responsive to pause/stop.
acceptance_criteria: FitnessProblem supports async batch evaluation and all 5 existing problems work with no source changes; the engine awaits fitness exactly once per generation, not once per individual; a rejected batch transitions the run to error status with the reason rather than hanging; pause and stop during an in-flight evaluation neither deadlock nor double-apply a generation; the existing 36 core tests still pass and new tests cover the async and rejection paths

title: Evolve PNG images toward a text prompt using a CLIP fitness evaluator
description: Add a GA problem that evolves raster images toward a text prompt. DECISIONS ALREADY MADE, do not re-litigate: (1) Genome is a RAW PIXEL BIT STRING, reusing the existing binary encoding and bit-flip mutation unchanged. (2) Fitness is CLIP image-text cosine similarity computed IN THE BROWSER via transformers.js on WebGPU and returned to the server over the existing WS channel - no model weights on the server. (3) Moondream is validation only: it runs every N generations on the best genome alone to give a human-readable progress check, and never in the per-individual path. CLIP supplies the gradient because it is continuous and climbable; a captioner is not, since early noise images all caption identically and the fitness landscape is flat. (4) Scores are cached by genome hash, which makes a replay of a run exact even though inference itself is not deterministic, and means elites cloned by elitism are never re-scored. KNOWN RISKS: a run cannot progress with no browser attached; 64x64 RGB is 98304 bits per genome; population 40 is roughly 491 KB per generation over a WS whose maxPayload is currently 1 MB; and the search space makes convergence genuinely uncertain, which the final spike bead measures rather than assumes.

title: Runs do not survive a server restart
description: RunManager holds live engines in an in-memory Map. A server restart destroys every engine while its SQLite row still reads status='running', so the UI shows a running experiment that is not running, and any control call (pause/resume/step/stop) returns 404 RunNotFoundError. There is no rehydration path. This is the single largest gap between what the persistence layer claims and what the system can actually do, and it is invisible in local dev where the server rarely restarts mid-run. Decide between rehydrating engines from persisted config+seed on boot (the run is reproducible from seed, so this is feasible) or marking orphaned runs as 'error'/'stopped' at startup so the UI stops lying. Documented as a known sharp edge in docs/architecture.md.
acceptance_criteria: After a server restart, no run is left claiming status 'running' when no engine backs it; either the run resumes or it is transitioned to a terminal status with a reason; a test covers the restart path; docs/architecture.md sharp-edge entry updated to match the new behavior
close_reason: RunManager now reconciles interrupted runs on boot: any row left pending/running/paused is closed out as 'stopped' with a persisted stopReason. Also fixed two adjacent bugs found while doing it — user-stopped runs persisted as 'finished', and server close left engines writing to a closed DB. Three regression tests, each verified against the old behavior.

title: Prepare repo for parallel agentic factory operation
description: Three gaps block running multiple agents concurrently. (1) NO CI: every gate so far ran on an agent's local machine and was self-reported; nothing verifies a PR server-side, which does not survive N agents opening PRs. (2) .beads/issues.jsonl conflicts structurally on every pair of concurrent branches since every bead rewrites it. (3) The loop protocol and Operating Mode assume one agent at a time and do not cover worktree isolation, port collisions, or self-directed work selection.
acceptance_criteria: GitHub Actions workflow runs all four gates on pull_request and push to master; .gitattributes + merge driver regenerates the beads export from the Dolt DB instead of conflicting; CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md document the parallel loop protocol, isolation requirements, and the self-directed charter; branch protection requires the CI check on master
close_reason: CI workflow running all four gates on PR and master; .gitattributes + beads-export merge driver verified against a real conflict; parallel loop protocol, self-directed charter, and isolation rules documented in CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md. Branch protection to be enabled after this merges (the check must exist first).

title: Wire up a real lint gate across all packages
description: Root package.json runs 'turbo run lint' but no package defines a lint script, so 'pnpm lint' exits green having executed nothing. In an autonomous loop this reports a passed quality gate that never ran. Add ESLint flat config + typescript-eslint at the root, add a lint script to all 4 packages (core, server, shared-types, web), and make turbo aware of the task.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm lint executes a real linter in all 4 packages; a deliberately introduced violation causes a non-zero exit; turbo.json declares the lint task
close_reason: Real lint gate wired up across all 4 packages; verified it fails closed on a deliberate violation. PR #1.

title: architectural documentation
description: Produce an architecture document covering two levels: (1) REPO ARCHITECTURE — monorepo layout, the four packages and their dependency direction, pnpm/turbo build pipeline and task graph, quality gates, and how beads issue tracking fits the workflow. (2) CODE ARCHITECTURE — how the GA engine is actually structured: the operator/registry abstraction and its extension points, the run lifecycle, the server's streaming model and WS protocol, and the web app's data flow. Aimed at a contributor who needs to add an operator or trace a run end to end.
acceptance_criteria: Doc covers both repo-level and code-level architecture; dependency direction between the 4 packages is stated explicitly; the operator extension path is documented well enough to add a new operator without reading the whole engine; the WS protocol and run lifecycle are described; all claims verified against the actual source, not inferred
close_reason: Architecture doc written covering repo architecture (packages, dependency direction, build pipeline, gates, issue workflow) and code architecture (operator/registry abstraction, run lifecycle, determinism, server streaming, WS protocol, web data flow), plus an operator extension guide and known sharp edges. All claims verified against source.

title: Diversity metric cost is prohibitive at very large genomes
description: A core engine performance issue, independent of any epic - large genomes merely expose it. GeneticAlgorithmEngine.computeDiversity samples up to 50 individuals and computes pairwise encoding.distance across them, which is 1225 pairs every generation. For the binary encoding that distance is a Hamming distance over the whole genome. At a 64x64 RGB image genome of 98304 bits that is roughly 120 million bit comparisons per generation, which will dominate the loop and has nothing to do with fitness or evaluators. Measure it first at a realistic genome size, then reduce: sampling bit positions rather than comparing whole genomes, caching per-genome contributions, or scaling the sample size to genome length are all plausible. Do NOT simply delete the metric - diversity is the signal that reveals population collapse, which matters more in a huge search space, not less.
acceptance_criteria: a benchmark records computeDiversity cost before and after at 98304-bit genomes; diversity remains a useful signal, demonstrated by correlating the reduced metric against the exact one on a genome small enough to compute both; existing core tests pass

title: Document externalized evaluation in the architecture doc
description: docs/architecture.md currently states that fitness is a synchronous in-process function and that every operator is one of six kinds - both become false with this epic, and a doc that lies is worse than one that is merely thin. Add an evaluator section covering the seventh registry kind, the contract-versus-capability split that keeps RunConfig portable, the job lifecycle from enqueue through claim, lease, submit and re-dispatch, and the generational barrier with its straggler consequence. Extend the operator extension guide, which currently walks through adding a selection operator, with the equivalent walkthrough for adding an evaluator and a worker. Update the six-kinds table and the sharp edges list. Also revisit the determinism section: it currently states flatly that the same seed and config produce an identical run, which stops being unconditionally true once an evaluator can be non-deterministic - the score cache is what restores it for replays, and that nuance belongs in the doc.
acceptance_criteria: the architecture doc describes evaluator as a seventh kind with the contract-versus-capability split, the job lifecycle including leases and re-dispatch, and the straggler consequence of the generational barrier; the extension guide covers adding an evaluator and a worker; the determinism section states precisely when reproducibility holds and when only cached replay does; every claim verified against the code as written, not as designed

title: Observability for distributed evaluation
description: A distributed generational system cannot be operated blind, and every failure mode in this epic looks identical from outside: the run just stops advancing. Whether that is a missing worker, an expired lease being re-dispatched in a loop, a single straggler holding the barrier, or a cache that is never hitting, is indistinguishable without instrumentation. Surface queue depth, connected workers and their capabilities, per-generation wall-clock split between queue wait and scoring, cache hit rate, lease expiry and re-dispatch counts, and straggler identification - which worker or job is holding the current barrier open. Straggler visibility matters most: the generational barrier means the slowest claim sets the pace, so knowing WHICH claim is slow is the difference between tuning the system and guessing at it.
acceptance_criteria: queue depth, connected workers with capabilities, cache hit rate, and lease expiry/re-dispatch counts are all observable; per-generation timing distinguishes queue wait from scoring time; the run view identifies which outstanding job or worker is holding a generation barrier open; a run making no progress can be diagnosed from these signals alone without reading server logs

title: Browser tab as a worker over WebSocket
description: The capability that originally motivated all of this: a browser tab registers as a worker and contributes WebGPU inference to a run. By this point it is a transport adapter, not an architecture - it speaks the same claim, lease, submit and heartbeat protocol as a worker thread, just over WS instead of in-process. Browser workers are inherently unreliable: tabs get closed, backgrounded, and throttled by the browser when not visible. That unreliability is already handled by lease expiry and re-dispatch, which is precisely why those were made mandatory rather than optional. Mind the payload - a population of 40 at 64x64 RGB is roughly 491 KB per generation against a maxPayload currently set to 1 MB. Nothing should break if the tab closes mid-claim except that another worker picks the jobs up.
acceptance_criteria: a browser tab registers as a worker, claims jobs and returns scores that a run consumes; closing the tab mid-claim causes re-dispatch and the run continues, covered by a test; a backgrounded or throttled tab does not stall a generation beyond lease expiry; server workers and browser workers can serve the SAME run concurrently; payload stays under maxPayload or maxPayload is raised deliberately with the arithmetic explained

title: Spike: does a raw bit string actually converge under CLIP-guided selection?
description: An honest measurement rather than an assumption, and the result may change the epic. A 64x64 RGB genome is 98304 bits, a search space of 2^98304, and CLIP scores of early random-noise images are both low and nearly indistinguishable, so there may be almost no gradient for selection to climb. Mutation rate needs rethinking too: the default of 0.01 flips roughly 983 bits per genome per generation, which is closer to randomisation than mutation, so something nearer 1e-4 is likely required. Run a fixed evaluation budget at a small resolution such as 32x32 with a simple high-contrast prompt, and compare the best CLIP score achieved against a random-search baseline given exactly the same number of evaluations - if evolution cannot beat random search, the encoding is not viable and no amount of tuning hides that. If it does not converge, evaluate at least one alternative encoding for comparison: palette-indexed pixels, which keeps the bit-string genome but cuts it roughly 6x and makes each mutation perceptually meaningful, or translucent vector primitives, which is the classic evolving-Mona-Lisa approach and converges far better because one mutation changes an entire shape. Report numbers, not impressions.
acceptance_criteria: a documented result stating whether CLIP-guided evolution of a raw bit string beats a random-search baseline on an equal evaluation budget; recommended default mutationRate, populationSize, and resolution for image runs, with the evidence behind them; if raw bit strings do not converge, a measured comparison against at least one alternative encoding and a recommendation

title: Export the best genome as a PNG
description: Producing a PNG is the literal point of the epic, and nothing in the pipeline actually emits one - raw pixel bytes go to the browser for scoring and to a canvas for display, deliberately, because PNG-encoding in the hot loop is wasted work. Export is the one place a real PNG belongs. sharp is already a workspace dependency and turns a raw pixel buffer into a PNG directly, so no new dependency is needed. Provide an endpoint and a UI action to download the best genome of a run at its current dimensions.
acceptance_criteria: an endpoint returns a valid PNG of the correct dimensions for a given run; it works for a finished run, a stopped run, and a run still in progress; the exported PNG is pixel-identical to what the canvas displays for the same generation; a run with no completed generation yet returns a clear error rather than an empty or corrupt file

title: Diversity metric cost is prohibitive at 98k-bit genomes
description: Independent of the model work, and it will bite the moment an image run starts. GeneticAlgorithmEngine.computeDiversity samples up to 50 individuals and computes pairwise encoding.distance across them, which is 1225 pairs per generation. For the binary encoding that distance is a Hamming distance over the entire genome. At 64x64 RGB the genome is 98304 bits, so diversity alone costs roughly 120 million bit comparisons per generation - likely dominating the loop and having nothing whatsoever to do with the fitness model. Measure it first at a realistic genome size, then reduce: sampling bit positions rather than comparing the whole genome, caching per-genome contributions, or making the sample size adaptive to genome length are all plausible. Do not simply delete the metric - diversity is the signal that tells you the population has collapsed, which matters more in a huge search space, not less.
acceptance_criteria: a benchmark records the cost of computeDiversity before and after at 98304-bit genomes; diversity remains a useful signal, demonstrated by correlating the reduced metric against the exact one on a genome small enough to compute both; existing core tests still pass

title: Periodic moondream validation pass on the best genome
description: A CLIP cosine similarity is a number with no human meaning - 0.19 tells you nothing about whether the run is going anywhere. Running moondream on the best genome every N generations produces a caption you can actually read, which is the point of the hybrid choice for this epic. Configurable interval, default every 25 generations, best genome ONLY. It must never enter the per-individual path: that is what makes a captioner unusable as the fitness signal, and putting it there would reintroduce exactly the flat-landscape problem this design avoids. Surface the caption in the run view alongside the generation it describes.
acceptance_criteria: a caption appears in the UI attached to the generation it describes; moondream runs on the best genome only and at most every N generations; failing to load or run moondream degrades gracefully and CLIP-driven evolution continues uninterrupted; the interval is configurable through the problem params and therefore through the auto-generated form

title: WebSocket unsubscribe drops every subscription on the socket
description: In server.ts the ws 'unsubscribe' handler clears ALL subscriptions held by that socket rather than just the named runId — the code calls it the 'cheap approach' and expects the client to resubscribe to anything else it still wants. Today the UI watches one run per socket so nothing breaks, but it blocks any live multi-run view: a comparison page that streams two runs would silently lose one the moment it unsubscribed from the other. Fix by tracking unsubscribe callbacks per runId instead of a flat Set.
acceptance_criteria: Unsubscribing from one runId leaves other subscriptions on the same socket intact; a server test subscribes to two runs, unsubscribes from one, and asserts events still arrive for the other; docs/architecture.md sharp-edge entry removed or updated
close_reason: WS subscriptions now tracked per runId in a Map: unsubscribe tears down only the named run, and re-subscribing replaces rather than stacks (a second latent bug in the same block). Two regression tests added, each verified to fail against the old behavior.

title: Test files are excluded from tsconfig, so typecheck does not cover them
description: packages/core/tsconfig.json and packages/server/tsconfig.json both 'exclude' src/**/*.test.ts so tests are not emitted into dist. A side effect nobody intended: 'pnpm typecheck' never type-checks test files, and typescript-eslint's project service cannot resolve them either (forcing type-aware lint rules off for tests). A test can therefore contain a type error and every gate stays green; only vitest's own transpile would notice, and it does not type-check. Fix with a separate tsconfig that includes tests and is referenced by the typecheck script and by eslint's project service.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm typecheck covers test files in all 4 packages; a deliberate type error in a test file fails the typecheck gate; type-aware lint rules can be re-enabled for tests in eslint.config.mjs
close_reason: tsconfig.json now includes test files in all packages; core/server build via a separate tsconfig.build.json that excludes them. Surfaced and fixed 3 pre-existing type errors in test files that no gate had ever seen. Type-aware lint re-enabled for tests. Verified a deliberate type error in a test fails typecheck, and dist emits no test files.

title: No test coverage for apps/web and packages/shared-types
description: Only core (36 tests) and server (5 tests) have vitest suites. apps/web and packages/shared-types define no test script, so the test gate cannot catch regressions there. The web visualizer can break with all gates green.
acceptance_criteria: Both packages have a test script wired into turbo; at least smoke-level coverage of the web app's rendering and the shared type contracts
close_reason: Test coverage added for both packages: web 37 runtime tests under jsdom, shared-types 21 type-level contract tests. Both verified to fail closed.

title: Enable type-aware ESLint rules
description: The lint gate added in genebaer-n2y uses typescript-eslint's non-type-checked recommended set for speed and setup simplicity. Type-aware rules (no-floating-promises, no-misused-promises, await-thenable, strict-boolean-expressions) catch a materially different and more valuable class of bug, especially in packages/server where async streaming lives. Enable via projectService once the base gate is stable.
acceptance_criteria: eslint.config.mjs uses recommendedTypeChecked with projectService; pnpm lint still passes; a deliberate floating promise is caught
close_reason: Type-aware rules enabled via recommendedTypeChecked + projectService. Surfaced and fixed 5 no-misused-promises and 1 no-floating-promises in web (real unhandled-rejection paths), 7 unnecessary assertions, and 16 unsafe-any assignments in core. Also fixed a turbo cache bug that made the lint gate serve stale results when the root config changed.
